title: Hardness of Pathfinding in a Welded Tree
abstract: Starting from the entrance of a welded tree, a quantum walk algorithm can find its exit vertex exponentially faster than any classical algorithm. However, it has been an open question whether any quantum algorithm is able to efficiently find a path from the entrance to the exit. We answer this by proving an exponential quantum query lower bound for finding such path. Specifically, for trees of height $n$, any quantum query algorithm requires at least $Ω(2^{n/24})$ queries in order to succeed with constant probability.   Our proof uses the compressed permutation oracle technique in order to construct databases which track the graph information an algorithm has learned and forgotten, and show that no efficient quantum algorithm can build an entrance-to-exit path in these records.
summary: This paper proves a strong quantum query lower bound for finding a path between two points in a welded tree graph. By employing advanced techniques involving compressed permutation oracles, the authors demonstrate that the required number of queries grows exponentially with the height of the tree. This result contrasts with known quantum speedups for simply locating the exit vertex.
main_problem: The paper addresses the open question of whether an efficient quantum algorithm exists to output a path from an entrance to an exit vertex in a welded tree graph.
main_result: The authors prove an exponential quantum query lower bound, showing that any quantum algorithm requires at least $\Omega(2^{n/24})$ queries to find the path with constant probability.
method: The proof utilizes the compressed permutation oracle technique within a recording/compressed oracle framework to construct databases tracking learned graph information.
model_or_system: The model is a welded tree graph ($G_n$), which is constructed from two binary trees whose leaves are joined by a cycle. The analysis focuses on the query complexity of algorithms operating on this graph structure.
key_observables: Query complexity (lower bound $\Omega(N^{1/24})$), success probability of path output ($O(q^6 N^{-1/4})$), and the state of the recorded information in databases $(L, C)$.
important_parameters: Graph height $n$, number of queries $q$, and the size of the graph $N$.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on constructing a 'fresh oracle' ($\hat{	ext{cpWT}}$) and uses techniques from previous work regarding compressed query operators.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the welded tree graph with marked entrance, exit, and leaves. Figure 2 provides an example of a fresh query, distinguishing between recorded information and available/forbidden connections.
paper_structure: The paper develops the proof by first establishing necessary lemmas regarding the difference between compressed and uncompressed query operators (using block partitions), and then applying these bounds to the specific structure of the welded tree to derive the final exponential lower bound for pathfinding.
why_interesting: The work establishes a fundamental quantum query lower bound for pathfinding in a structured graph, providing a theoretical limit on the efficiency of quantum computation for graph traversal problems.
